subject: Request: Comparative onboarding and concession analysis for GlacialTech migration
messages:
From: Maya Lind <procurement@glacialtech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Comparative onboarding and concession analysis for GlacialTech migration

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look — we are running a short evaluation of vendors as part of a Q4 migration. Attached is our RFP (summary tab) with usage bands and must-have items (SOC2, VPC, key rotation).

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood provide a competitive price match or structured concession that gets us within 10% of the incumbent’s blended price?
- What onboarding credits and hands-on migration support do you offer for a multi-month migration (we estimate ~18M tokens/mo in steady state)?

We have a procurement cadence next week and it would be great to understand a credible concession framework and rough TCO quickly — ideally a one-pager we can share internally.

Attaching: GlacialTech_RFP_Sheet.xlsx

Best,
Maya Lind
Head of Procurement
GlacialTech
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lind <procurement@glacialtech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Comparative onboarding and concession analysis for GlacialTech migration

Hi Maya — thanks for sending the RFP and context. I copied Jordan (sales ops) to make sure we align on margin / credit mechanics. Quick responses below and a proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to align on bands and incumbent numbers.

What we can do now (high level):
- Concession levers we typically use: one-time onboarding credit, time-limited tiered discounts for committed volume, and paid migration hours (or included work) with a transition SLA.
- Example starter offer we can run internally: ~15–20% off list for Year 1 (scaled by committed token bands) + a one-time onboarding credit sized to the migration effort.
- We’ll also accelerate onboarding (engineer-led runbook, 2-week pilot support) to shorten cutover risk.

To give a sharper number for procurement, we need the incumbent blended rate per token and the desired target (within 10% of incumbent is helpful). Can you share the incumbent offer or a target $/1k tokens?

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick call: Wed 9/8 at 11:00 AM PDT or Thu 9/9 at 2:00 PM PDT — which works?
2) If you can share the incumbent blended $/1k, we’ll put a one-pager (pricing + onboarding credit + timeline) on the call.

I attached a one-pager outline we usually start from (Onboarding_Timeline_v2.pdf) that covers milestones and typical credit sizing.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Comparative onboarding and concession analysis for GlacialTech migration

Irene — quick internal note before we respond publicly.

Parameters to keep in mind:
- GlacialTech scale (~18M tokens/mo steady) gives us leverage on committed pricing, but they’re sensitive to headline ARR impact.
- We have 12–15% gross margin headroom on large committed deals before the offering gets non-standard (excludes infra pass-through).

Concession framework I’d recommend we propose to Procurement (keeps the win probability high while protecting model economics):
1) Pilot & onboarding credit: $35k one-time credit applied against deployment/migration invoicing (covers 2 FTE-weeks of engineering support + runbook customization).
2) Year-1 blended discount: 18% off list (applies to first 12 months, tiered by volume band).
3) Migration SLA & discounted overage: first 60 days post-cutover, overage billed at 60% of list rate.
4) Commitment term: 12 months with a short escape clause if monthly usage < 60% of forecast for 3 consecutive months.

If the incumbent's blended is within ~10% of list after the 18% discount + credit (they often fail to account for onboarding costs), we should be able to close without additional exec credits. If procurement pushes for deeper discount we can escalate a one-time retention credit but prefer to avoid as it sets a precedent.

I'll build a quick TCO calc we can attach. If you want to be more aggressive up-front, we can surface a $50k credit option but mark it as leadership approval required.

—Jordan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Lind <procurement@glacialtech.com>, Daniel Park <ops@glacialtech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Comparative onboarding and concession analysis for GlacialTech migration

Hi Maya / Daniel — following our call earlier today, here’s the proposal we agreed to put on the table for your procurement review. I’ve kept it concise for easy internal sharing.

Summary proposal for GlacialTech (draft)
- One-time onboarding credit: $35,000 applied to migration/integration invoices (covers runbook work and 2 FTE-weeks of engineer support).
- Year-1 blended discount: 18% off published list rates, applied across committed token bands for the first 12 months.
- Migration protection: first 60 days post-cutover, overages billed at 60% of list rate; standard monitoring & 24/7 escalation for first 30 days.
- Commitment term: 12 months with an operational performance clause (escape if usage < 60% of forecast for 3 consecutive months).

Quick notes:
- This structure keeps the headline discount competitive while neutralizing migration costs that incumbents hide in professional services.
- If Procurement needs a deeper headline, Jordan indicated we can escalate to Leadership for a one-time retention credit (up to $50k) but that requires approval and will be treated as exceptional.

Attachments: Onboarding_Timeline_v2.pdf (timeline and milestones), GlacialTech_RFP_Sheet.xlsx (for our reference)

Next step: Please confirm if this is sufficient for your procurement packet. If yes, we’ll prepare a short commercial addendum and send for signature (DocuSign link to follow). If you want the more aggressive $50k option, let us know and we’ll route for approval immediately.

Thanks again — happy to hop back on a quick call if procurement needs a walkthrough.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
